title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study (Revision)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) comparing a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N=120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks evaluated by a deterministic validator. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics all confirmatory episodes completed and both conditions passed the verifier on all tasks (baseline 120/120; guarded 120/120). Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Using the archived execution artifacts we (i) publish the exact per‑file paths and SHA‑256 fingerprints required for exact reproduction, (ii) diagnose—on the basis of those artifacts—why the paired outcome is uninformative about independent generative reliability (the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design combined with template‑tight tasks and a deterministic validator), and (iii) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity, task heterogeneity) that yield informative independent comparisons without inventing new data. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction:
Automating network operations (NetOps) from high‑level intent into device configurations is an active research and deployment goal. Large language models (LLMs) offer promise for intent translation, but semantic correctness (reachability, access control, ordering, transient safety) is safety‑critical. Verifier‑grounded evaluation—using deterministic validators to test semantic properties—has emerged as a best practice for operational validation (e.g., Batfish and related verifier tooling [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]).

We preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to answer a single question: under a verifier‑grounded paired design, does a single‑pass LLM generator produce a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline on programmatic synthetic intent→configuration tasks? The preregistration and execution artifacts were frozen before running the study (preregistration SHA‑256 above). This revision responds to peer review by (a) adding high‑visibility caution language about the confirmatory semantics, (b) publishing exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 fingerprints for reproducibility, and (c) expanding the artifact‑grounded methodological diagnosis and runnable follow‑ups.
sections.related_work:
Verifier‑based NetOps tools (Batfish and successors) demonstrate that deterministic analysis greatly reduces misconfiguration risk and can scale to real networks [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent LLM→NetOps work focuses on intent translation and generate–validate–repair pipelines; authors note token‑level metrics poorly reflect operational correctness, motivating verifier‑centric evaluation [https://doi.org/10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407, https://doi.org/10.1002/nem.70029].

Our submission differs: rather than proposing a new generator or benchmark, we preregister and release a complete execution and analysis bundle whose design choices (notably the confirmatory generation semantics) are transparent and auditable. The run is intended as an exemplar of artifact‑anchored preregistration for LLM→NetOps evaluation rather than a claim of broad model superiority or operational readiness.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered study (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) specified a paired confirmatory test (H1) with estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline across N=120 programmatic tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS). Primary inference used paired_binary_analysis_v1 with 10,000 bootstrap resamples (bootstrap_seed=1729) to produce percentile CIs. Exploratory analyses (seed sensitivity, rank stability) were predeclared but do not affect the confirmatory claim.

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were deterministically synthesized from template bank code (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, version 5.0). Each task payload encodes: (i) initial_state and expected_final_state, (ii) required_sequence (canonical command sequence), (iii) workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), and (iv) allowed_touched_fields. Representative task entries are archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl and appear verbatim in the manifest entries published with the execution bundle. Inclusion rule in the preregistration required that any gold‑template failing unit tests (parse or baseline verifier) be excluded and replaced to preserve N=120.

Confirmatory generation semantics (critical preregistered choice). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate": for each pair a single canonical candidate (seed_0) was produced and the identical candidate was evaluated both as the deterministic template baseline and as the guarded (gpt‑5‑mini) episode. This design isolates validator behavior across conditions but does not test independent sampling variability of generators. The shared candidate artifacts and provider trace files are archived (paths and SHA‑256s below). The Research Director approved topic constraints before autonomy lock; after the lock the autonomous pipeline executed generation, validation, analysis, manuscript drafting, and revision.

Model, adapter, and validator. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation; per‑episode scoring JSONs include normalized_response, validator_trace (validation_before/after), parsed_command_count and a binary score. All scoring artifacts archived under execution/scoring/*.json.

Execution accounting, retries, and reproducibility. Planned_episode_count=240; completed_episode_count=240; failed_episode_count=0; model_calls_used=120; run timestamps and full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are in execution/execution_manifest.json (see artifact list below). A contamination heuristic (exact match + 5‑gram overlap thresholds) was executed as preregistered; its summary is in analysis/contamination_summary.csv.
sections.results:
Confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded). All confirmatory episodes completed; the paired contingency table is degenerate: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaafb3...). Both conditions passed the validator on all tasks: baseline_success_count=120/120; guarded_success_count=120/120. The paired difference (mean over tasks of guarded_i−baseline_i)=0.00. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.00, 0.00] and exact McNemar two‑sided p=1.0; these inferential outputs and seeds are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA‑256 ff20bc07...).

Representative per‑task diagnostic evidence (artifact pointers and hashes). To support immediate audit and exact reproduction we include the canonical file paths and SHA‑256 fingerprints for a small, representative subset of artifacts used in the diagnosis (these files are present in the execution bundle and their hashes match the packed manifest):
- Preregistration (frozen): preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37 (execution manifest references this value). 
- Initial master prompt (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
- Representative shared_initial candidate and responses (pair‑000001): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080. The identical file appears as baseline and guarded responses for that pair (see execution/responses/task-000001-baseline.txt and execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt; identical SHA‑256).
- Representative scoring trace (pair‑000001 guarded): execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57fff893fe02bd395c435a422f5431376e439875577a8431063. This JSON contains validator_trace.validation_after with parsed_command_count=4, required_command_count=4, violation_count=0 and the validator final_state matching the expected_final_state in the task manifest.
- Execution manifest and full manifest path: execution/execution_manifest.json (contains exhaustive per‑file SHA‑256 listing used for deterministic reconciliation). 

Contamination checks. The preregistered string‑overlap contamination heuristic reported no confirmatory flags under the pre‑specified thresholds. The contamination summary artifact is analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA‑256 389227f0d1e8...). Publicly available artifact hashes allow independent verification that the same files were used to generate the reported numbers.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded diagnosis of the degenerate paired outcome. The archival evidence shows three decisive and interacting causes that make the paired outcome uninformative about independent generative reliability: 
1) Shared‑candidate confirmatory semantics (preregistered): each pair used a single canonical candidate (seed_0) supplied identically to both the baseline and guarded episodes (evidence: execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt and execution/provider_calls/*-shared-initial.json). This design answers whether a validator treats an identical artifact differently across conditions, but not whether two different generators produce artifacts with differing pass probabilities under independent sampling. 
2) Template‑tight synthetic tasks: task payloads encode deterministic required_sequence and workflow_policies that admit an obvious canonical solution; template unit tests were required for inclusion (evidence: execution/task_manifest.jsonl entries with required_sequence and workflow_policies). 
3) Deterministic validator coupling to task templates: the validator enforces the template constraints and declares a candidate valid when it matches required_sequence semantic constraints (evidence: execution/scoring/*.json validator_trace fields showing parsed_command_count equals required_command_count and violation_count=0 for passing pairs). 

Together, these create a matched condition in which a single canonical candidate validates equally in both arms, producing n_11=N. The numeric inferential outputs (p=1.0, CI [0.00,0.00]) are arithmetically correct but substantively uninformative about independent model reliability because the confirmatory sampling removed generative independence. This diagnosis is fully supported by the archived artifacts and file hashes cited above.

Runnable, artifact‑grounded corrective modifications. Using only the provided execution bundle and the published task generator code, the following changes are immediately implementable and will produce informative independent comparisons: 
A. independent_per_condition confirmatory sampling — modify the generation stage to produce one independent candidate per condition per pair (i.e., generate a baseline_candidate and a guarded_candidate instead of a shared candidate). This change is implemented by editing the adapter configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) to set generation_semantics="independent_per_condition" and re‑running the archived pipeline using the published task manifest. 
B. multi‑seed confirmatory design — sample K>1 independent seeds per condition for each task and estimate per‑condition pass probability (the preregistration already described exploratory seeds_1..4; move them into confirmatory design). 
C. validator diversification — add a second, independent validator (for example an emulation‑based reachability analyzer) and report intersection/union pass rates; per‑episode validators are JSON‑logged in execution/scoring/*.json enabling easy addition of a second adjudicator. 
D. task heterogeneity — expand the template bank with paraphrase variants and randomized constraint perturbations so that canonical solutions are less deterministic; the deterministic task generator code (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) can be parameterized for wider sampling. 

Each of these modifications is executable using only the archived artifacts and code; no new data or unverifiable claims are required. We emphasize these changes because they directly address the confirmatory semantics that produced the degenerate result; the execution manifest contains the paths needed to rerun (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released a complete, hash‑verified artifact bundle. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and guarded conditions validated on all N=120 synthetic tasks (both 120/120). Artifact evidence (shared candidates, scoring traces, task manifests) shows that identical per‑pair canonical candidates and template‑tight tasks drove the degenerate contingency table. Consequently the confirmatory paired test, as preregistered, does not measure independent LLM generative robustness in operational sampling. We publish exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 fingerprints so others can (i) reproduce the run exactly, (ii) reconfigure generation semantics to independent_per_condition or multi‑seed confirmatory designs, and (iii) re‑execute with validator diversification and broader task heterogeneity to obtain informative independent comparisons. All numeric claims, paths, and hashes above are taken verbatim from the archived execution and analysis artifacts. We do not invent additional experiments, data, or statistics beyond those artifacts.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not part of the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
